project.title: Liver-specific paraoxonase-1 alleviates regulatory T cell-driven immunosuppression via metabolic reprogramming in hepatocellular carcinoma
project.projectDescription: Paraoxonase-1 (PON1) is specifically expressed in the liver and has crucial effects on various liver diseases. The functions and mechanisms underlying of PON1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain obscure. Here, we show that PON1 acts as a metabolic regulator to mitigate regulatory T (Treg) cell-induced immunosuppression and HCC progression. Mechanistically, PON1 crippled lactic acid generation via recruiting Von Hippel-Lindau protein (VHL) to ubiquitinate Hypoxia-inducible factor alpha (HIF-1α), thereby reducing Treg cell frequency in HCC. In clinical settings, high PON1 expression correlated with better prognosis in HCC patients. Recombinant PON1 protein (rPON1) exhibited remarkable potency in impeding tumor growth, meanwhile, enhancing PON1 expression by Quercetin sensitized HCC to anti-programmed death-1(PD-1) therapy. Our findings elucidate a novel role of PON1 in orchestrating lactic acid production to relieve immunosuppression and suppress HCC, which paves the way for therapeutic intervention of HCC by targeting PON1.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: For each sample, an appropriate amount of peptide segments was taken and subjected to chromatographic separation using the Vanquish Neo UHPLC system (Thermo Scientific). The buffers were as follows: Solution A was an aqueous solution of 0.1% formic acid, and Solution B was an aqueous solution of 0.1% formic acid and acetonitrile (with 80% acetonitrile). The chromatographic column was equilibrated with 96% Solution A. The sample was injected into the Trap Column (PepMap Neo 5 µm C18, 300 µm X 5 mm, Thermo Scientific) and then underwent gradient separation through the chromatographic analytical column (μPAC Neo High Throughput column, Thermo Scientific). The liquid - phase gradient was set as follows: from 0 min to 0.1 min, the linear gradient of Solution B was from 4% to 6%; from 0.1 min to 1.1 min, the linear gradient of Solution B was from 6% to 12%; from 1.1 min to 4.3 min, the linear gradient of Solution B was from 12% to 22.5%; from 4.3 min to 6.1 min, the linear gradient of Solution B was from 22.5% to 45%; from 6.1 min to 8 min, Solution B was maintained at 99%. After the peptide segments were separated, DIA (Data - Independent Acquisition) mass spectrometry analysis was carried out using an Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific). The analysis duration was 8 minutes, the electrospray voltage was 2.2 kV, the detection mode was positive ions, the parent ion scanning range was 380 - 980 m/z, the resolution of the first - stage mass spectrometry was 240,000, the AGC target was 500%, and the first - stage Maximum IT was 3 ms. The resolution of the second - stage mass spectrometry was 80,000, the AGC target was 500%, the second - stage Maximum IT was 3 ms, the RF - lens was 40%, the MS2 Activation Type was HCD, the Isolation window was 2 Th, the Normalized collision energy was 25%, and the cycle time was 0.6.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: To ensure the effectiveness and accuracy of subsequent bioinformatics and statistical analyses, in accordance with general principles, in the protein identification table, we first screened the sample experimental data. We ensured that for the proteins being identified, at least 50% of the data without null values were retained in the corresponding sample groups. Then, we filled in the remaining null values and carried out statistical analyses. Proteins that met the screening criteria of having a fold - change in expression greater than 2.0 (either up - or down - regulation) and a P - value less than 0.05 were regarded as significantly differentially expressed proteins.
